title: Look at Berlin at the borrowed eyes' native scale: the 128 px frame is resized in-graph to 224 px (ImageNet's training resolution) before the pretrained trunk, so its 8x8/4x4 place maps become 14x14/7x7
init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v3_small IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..10] (torchvision, BSD-3), unchanged from experiments 12-14
hypothesis: Builds directly on experiments 12-14, the only designs on this ruler that moved the held-out photograph: swapping in an ImageNet-pretrained trunk took truedop_2024 from 10.75% to 49.5% usable (exp 12), reading it two blocks deeper took it to 60.25% (exp 13), and mixing survey style inside it took it to 65.5% (exp 14, usable 0.655 / false fix 0.05 / abstain 0.295, mission 0.395). Every gain came from the pretrained trunk's invariance doing more of the work. Meanwhile the training photographs sit at 95.5-97% usable at the same held-out viewpoints (train_capture_diagnostics 0.058 / 0.033 / 0.043) and the clean survey diagnostic has stopped moving (xs_cos_same 0.657 -> 0.656, wpv 0.236 -> 0.240, xsurvey_agree 0.74 -> 0.72 from exp 13 to 14): MixStyle helped the score without making the embedding of a place any more survey-independent, so the remaining 30-point gap is the trunk not yet describing a place in survey-free terms. One thing about how the trunk is used has never been questioned: SCALE. MobileNetV3-Small learned its invariant features on 224 px images, but we feed it 128 px, so every filter sees structure at 0.57x the size it was trained on, its stem throws away half the resolution at the first layer (2 m per feature after the stem), and the deep 96-channel level we read is a 4x4 map — 16 samples of 32 m each, averaged into the place feature. Train/test resolution mismatch is a known, large effect on pretrained-feature transfer (Touvron et al., FixRes, NeurIPS 2019), and here it is compounded by the GAP over a tiny map: a single car, shadow or construction patch that differs between surveys owns 1/16 of the deep descriptor. Resizing the frame to 224 px in-graph changes no weights and adds no parameters: the same pretrained filters see roofs, street edges and tree crowns at the scale their invariance was learned at, and the place feature averages 196 (mid) and 49 (deep) cells instead of 64 and 16, diluting survey-specific transients. This is the input-scale/decode-resolution family, absent from all 97 experiments in either database.
method: ONE change, in model/model.py Member.embed(): the [0,1] 128x128 input is bilinearly resized to INPUT_PX = 224 (a fixed output size, in the exported graph) before ImageNet normalisation and the trunk. Trunk, lifts, MixStyle insertion points, cosine-prototype head, committee decode, losses, augmentation, schedule, epochs and the ONNX I/O contract are all unchanged. The trunk's maps at the two read levels become 48x14x14 (after block 8) and 96x7x7 (after block 10); GAP makes the place feature shape-agnostic, so EMBED_DIM stays 112 and the exported weights are byte-for-byte the same size.
expected_outcome: truedop_2024 usable 0.655 -> 0.70-0.76, false fix held at or below 0.05 (the min-over-members gate is untouched), abstain falling correspondingly: mission 0.395 -> ~0.29-0.34. Training-capture diagnostics stay near 0.03-0.06 (they are already saturated), so the memorisation-vs-ground gap should narrow by ~5-10 usable points. Survey diagnostic: xs_cos_same up from 0.656 toward 0.70+, wpv down from 0.24, xsurvey_agree up from 0.72-0.73 — if the score improves while these do not move, the gain came from finer spatial averaging rather than better invariance, which is still informative. Falsifier: if 2024 usable stays at or below 0.66 while the training captures hold, input scale is not the bottleneck and the next move is more/other pretrained capacity rather than resolution. Cost: ~3x trunk FLOPs; host latency proxy ~4 ms -> ~12-15 ms (gate 250 ms); model bytes unchanged (7.45 MB fp32); training on the g6 ~17 min -> ~40-50 min, an acceptable round. On-chip latency roughly triples too; at the 1-10 s fix schedule that is a cost worth measuring, not a blocker.
eli5: We borrowed a pair of eyes trained on a million everyday photos, but we have been showing them Berlin through a keyhole: our camera frames are about half the size of the pictures those eyes learned on, so every roof and street looks shrunken and blurry to them. This experiment simply enlarges each frame to the size the eyes are used to before they look. Nothing new is learned or added — the same eyes just get to see the city at the scale where they are good at telling what is permanent (the street grid, the buildings) from what changes between photo flights (cars, shadows, colours).

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: NEW: the 128 px frame is first enlarged to 224 px - the size the borrowed eyes were trained on - so roads, roofs and trees appear at the scale their skills were learned at. Then, as before: two independent copies of the first eleven blocks of MobileNetV3-Small, pre-trained on ImageNet (open BSD-3 licence) and fine-tuned on Berlin at a tenth of the usual learning rate. Each reads the frame at two depths, now as finer maps: a 48-channel 14×14 map (edges and textures) and a deeper 96-channel 7×7 map (how roads, roofs and trees are arranged across the frame). Each depth is lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame; the two halves together are the 112-number description of the place

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each) - a compass, not a lookup table; the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: unchanged from experiment 14: cross-survey style mixing inside the feature extractor after its 2nd, 4th and 7th blocks (training only), angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate; targets, epochs and views per epoch unchanged. Training views are enlarged to 224 px exactly as in flight

implementation_brief:
Single focused change: an in-graph input resize to the pretrained trunk's native resolution. Touch ONLY model/model.py (constant + Member.embed + docstring) and model/train.py (logging strings / train_info fields + docstring). Do not change anything else.

model/model.py:
1. Add a module constant next to TRUNK_BLOCKS: `INPUT_PX = 224  # frame is bilinearly resized to this before the pretrained trunk (ImageNet training resolution)`.
2. In Member.embed(x), as the FIRST operation, before ImageNet normalisation: `x = F.interpolate(x, size=(INPUT_PX, INPUT_PX), mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)` — use a FIXED `size=` tuple, not `scale_factor`, and do NOT pass antialias=True (upsampling; keep the ONNX Resize op plain, opset 17). Then `xn = (x - self.in_mean) / self.in_std` and the rest of embed() exactly as now: the block loop, MixStyle after MIXSTYLE_AFTER = (1, 3, 6) in training mode, h_mid taken after block index TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS - 1 (now [B,48,14,14]), h_deep after the last block (now [B,96,7,7]), both lifts, GAP via .mean(dim=(2,3)), concat to EMBED_DIM=112, embed_bn, L2-normalise. Update the inline shape comments ([B, 48, 14, 14], [B, 96, 7, 7]). No other code change in model.py: Member.forward, CellLocNet (committee decode, block_mask, min-over-members conf, centroid + mean offset), MixStyle, loss_fn (COS_SCALE=30, COS_MARGIN=0.25), build_pretrained_trunk, export_onnx all untouched. EMBED_DIM, LIFT_DIM, TRUNK_* constants untouched; the pretrained file mnv3s_features10.pt is still loaded strict.
3. Add a docstring paragraph 'NATIVE-SCALE INPUT (capture-holdout era, experiment 15)': the 128 px frame is resized in-graph to INPUT_PX=224, MobileNetV3's ImageNet training resolution, so the pretrained filters see structure at the scale their invariance was learned at (FixRes-style train/test resolution matching) and the two read levels become 48x14x14 and 96x7x7; no new parameters; the external input contract stays 1x3x128x128.

model/train.py:
4. Import INPUT_PX from model.model. In the startup print add `input {CROP_PX}->{INPUT_PX} px bilinear (in-graph)` and change the lift shapes text to `@14x14` / `@7x7` (derive from INPUT_PX//16 and INPUT_PX//32 rather than hardcoding). In train_info add `"input_px": INPUT_PX`, append `, frame resized in-graph 128->224 px before the trunk` to the capture_sampling string, and update the `trunk` string's level shapes the same way. Add one docstring paragraph 'NATIVE-SCALE INPUT (experiment 15)' saying the resize lives in Member.embed, so training views, survey_diag and the export all see it identically. No change to gpu_crops (crops are still cut at CROP_PX=128 — the resize happens inside the model), augment_views/AUG (augmentation still runs on the 128 px crop, before the model), BATCH_SIZE=64, CHUNK_SIZE, the optimiser groups / TRUNK_LR_MULT / LambdaLR schedule, the committee loop, survey_diag, targets, or the CLI.
5. Memory: ~3x activation memory in the trunk. If, and only if, a smoke run OOMs on the device, keep BATCH_SIZE=64 and wrap nothing else — report it rather than changing the batch size silently; on the AWS g6 (24 GB L4) and the M1 batch 64 x 2 members at 224 px fits comfortably for MobileNetV3-Small.

Verification before exiting (implementation agent): (a) `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir /tmp/exp15_smoke --epochs 1` is NOT required in full, but do a quick forward/export check: build the model from load_meta('berlin'), run a [2,3,128,128] tensor through CellLocNet in eval mode, confirm output shape [2,3] and that member.embed's h_mid/h_deep are 14x14/7x7; export to ONNX and run it with onnxruntime on a 1x3x128x128 input; time ~20 runs and confirm the latency is far under 250 ms and the file is ~7.45 MB (≤ 32 MiB). (b) Confirm MixStyle is identity in eval mode (export unaffected). Use only the TRAINING captures if you touch data at all; never open truedop_2024 or any eval-capture file from model/.

Contracts to preserve (frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI unchanged — `python -m model.train --area <area> --out-dir <dir> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`; it writes <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out-dir>/train_info.json. ONNX: input name 'frame', 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1]; output name 'uvc', [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords in [0,1] and conf in [0,1]; the whole decode stays inside the graph; opset 17, dynamo=False. Training reads only buckets(meta, 'train'); nothing under model/ may open the eval capture truedop_2024 in any form. Gates: fp32 ONNX ≤ 32 MiB, host latency proxy ≤ 250 ms.
